# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview
Since both billing systems can run concurrently, this plan uses a phased, reversible migration strategy. The legacy system remains fully operational and untouched (no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning of any kind) throughout all user-migration phases, and only becomes a candidate for retirement in a dedicated phase after 100% of users are confirmed stable on the new system.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users, ~800 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including parallel invoice-generation reconciliation against the legacy system with 100% output parity on a synthetic dataset; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end; on-call rotation is staffed.

- Select low-risk, internal/friendly accounts (employee accounts, opt-in beta customers) plus a small random sample.
- Run both systems in parallel ("shadow mode") for these users: new system is billing of record, legacy system continues generating invoices in the background for diffing, but does not send to customers.
- Manually review every invoice, payment, and dunning event generated for this cohort.

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (15% of users, ~6,000 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed for a minimum of 14 days with zero critical billing discrepancies (defined as any invoice amount mismatch >$0.01 or failed payment capture) and support ticket volume from the pilot cohort no higher than the baseline rate for that segment.

- Expand to a broader, still-segmented population (e.g., single-region customers, monthly-billing-cycle customers only, excluding annual/enterprise contracts).
- Automated reconciliation replaces full manual review; manual review continues on a 10% sample.
- Customer communications begin (email notice of billing system update, no action required).

## Phase 3: General Availability (60% of users, ~24,000 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed for a minimum of 21 days with discrepancy rate below the halt threshold (see Metrics below), reconciliation automation validated against manual sample with 99.9%+ agreement, and customer support team trained/staffed for expected ticket volume.

- Migrate remaining standard-tier customers in waves of ~10% every 3–5 days, gated by the same discrepancy and support metrics.
- Legacy system remains live and continues serving not-yet-migrated users; no legacy functionality is reduced.

## Phase 4: Final Batch — Complex Accounts (23% of users, ~9,200 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative discrepancy rate below threshold for 30 consecutive days; all edge-case handling (proration, multi-currency, enterprise contracts, annual billing, credits/refunds) has been explicitly validated against this account segment in staging.

- Migrate remaining highest-complexity accounts (enterprise contracts, custom pricing, annual renewals, accounts with active disputes/credits).
- White-glove handling: dedicated account managers notified, migration scheduled outside each customer's billing-cycle boundary where possible.
- Legacy system remains fully operational and is **not** modified, disabled, or scheduled for decommissioning during this phase — it stays as the rollback path until Phase 4 stability is confirmed.

## Phase 5: Legacy Decommissioning (0% of users — infrastructure only)
**Entry criterion:** 100% of users migrated and stable on the new system for a minimum of 45 days with zero critical billing discrepancies in that window; finance has reconciled a full billing cycle end-to-end on the new system; explicit sign-off obtained from Finance, Engineering, and Compliance.

- Only in this phase does work begin on read-only archival of legacy data, followed by disabling write access, and eventual decommissioning — kept entirely separate from any user-migration activity.

---

## Halt Metric

**Halt the rollout immediately if the invoice discrepancy rate (mismatched or failed-to-generate invoices ÷ total invoices processed on the new system) exceeds 0.5% in any rolling 24-hour window**, or if payment capture failure rate for migrated users exceeds 1.0% in any rolling 24-hour window. Either trigger pauses further migration waves, freezes the affected cohort's billing on the new system (falling back to legacy for that cohort where feasible), and requires root-cause resolution plus sign-off before resuming.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges when both systems process the same billing cycle | Implement idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that flags any customer billed by both systems before charges settle | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data sync lag between old and new systems causes stale payment method or balance data | Use real-time or near-real-time bidirectional sync with monitoring/alerting on sync latency exceeding 5 minutes | Platform Infrastructure Team
RISK: Customer confusion or support overload from billing changes (new invoice format, login, etc.) | Proactive customer communication plan, updated help-center articles, and temporary support surge staffing during each phase | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Enterprise/custom-contract accounts have edge-case pricing logic not fully replicated in the new system | Dedicated QA pass and account-manager review for all enterprise accounts before Phase 4 migration | QA Lead
RISK: Rollback from new system back to legacy fails or loses data for a migrated cohort | Test and document a rollback runbook before each phase, including data-freeze windows and dual-write verification | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 5
